messages.subject: zero - truncated/hurdle model using INLA
parts:
Dear helpdesk,

Hope this post finds you well.

I am wondering if I can fit a zero-truncated/two-parts binary-poisson hurdle model in INLA using the family "zeroinflatedpoisson0" if i want to investigate a covariate effect for both the zero part and the non-zero part.

Thank you in advance for your time and help. I look forward to hearing from you soon.

Best,
Jocelyn

parts:
Hi,
Thank you Jocelyn for your initial question, I have had the same for some time.
I'm trying to use 0poisson on a dataset where I have a single outcome vector/column. My zeros are generated so that they best fit in a hurdle model. I want the zero-inflation probability and Poisson probability for each covariate as a fixed effect. I understand how to set this up using other families (e.g., zeroinflatedpoisson0), but not for 0poisson. I've attached an example of what my data looks like.
Also, Haavard, you mention implementing a two-likelihood model. Is that completed by specifying two families: family = c("binomial", "zeroinflatedpoisson0") like in this paper?

Thank you,
Kyle
